root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` calls `reader->parse(data_str, data_str + size, ...)`, the computed parser end pointer must stay within the real testcase allocation end tracked in `sAssertTrueInputEnd`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable harness advances `data` past the 4-byte settings header but leaves `size` unchanged, so the parse call still computes `data_str + size` as though the skipped bytes were part of the remaining payload. In the crashing run that bound extends four bytes past the true testcase allocation end. In the fixed program the same parse call executes with `data_str + size <= sAssertTrueInputEnd`.

nodes.state: At `Json::OurReader::parse`, member `end_` is materialized from the overstated parse span and therefore remains four bytes past the real testcase end.
At the `getNextChar()` dereference site, `current_` has advanced to the true testcase end tracked in `sAssertTrueInputEnd`, so dereferencing `*current_` reads the first byte beyond the allocation.

edges.relation: The parse-call end expression `data_str + size` is stored verbatim into `Json::OurReader::end_`, materializing the stale parser bound inside reader state.
The same stale `end_` value stored at parse entry remains the bound that `getNextChar()` uses at the sink, so the reader still treats bytes beyond the real testcase end as in-range.
